business_problem: Meesho's rapid growth and peak-sale traffic overwhelmed its self-managed Kafka infrastructure, creating downtime risk, limiting throughput, and preventing the company from using customer and purchase data in real time for personalization.
solution_summary: Meesho adopted Confluent Cloud as the core data-ingestion layer for its e-commerce ecosystem so it could re-architect around elastic real-time streams instead of manually scaled Kafka clusters. The managed platform now absorbs bursty traffic during major sale events, carries data from across the marketplace, and makes those streams available to downstream services without the operational drag of cluster maintenance and over-provisioning. Because customer and purchase events are available immediately, teams can use the streaming layer for new retail experiences such as a real-time recommendation engine rather than waiting for delayed historical datasets. Confluent's pay-as-you-go model also lets Meesho size for actual bandwidth and usage instead of peak guesses. Together, those capabilities help the company ship features faster, survive traffic spikes, and turn fresh marketplace data into more relevant offers and product suggestions for shoppers.

solution_components.name: Confluent Cloud
solution_components.role: Serves as Meesho's elastic ingestion and streaming backbone for sale events, marketplace data, and personalization workflows.

data_flow: Marketplace, customer, and purchase events stream into Confluent Cloud as the central ingestion layer, where downstream services consume them for peak-sale operations and for real-time recommendation and offer-generation use cases.
business_outcome: Meesho can now handle much larger sale-day traffic, deploy new services faster, lower infrastructure overhead, and personalize shopping experiences with a real-time recommendation engine backed by current customer data.
